subject: English
central_question: How does the loss of the right to learn one’s language transform an ordinary school day into a lesson about identity, regret and freedom?
in_scope_units: About the author and the Franco-Prussian War setting in Alsace and Lorraine.
Franz’s late journey to school, fear of participles and the unusual silence in the classroom.
The order from Berlin and the reactions of Franz, M. Hamel and the villagers.
M. Hamel’s teaching on shared responsibility, language and freedom.
The writing and history lessons and the final “Vive La France!” scene.
Understanding, discussion, vocabulary, past-perfect and writing activities.
banned_topics: A detailed military history of the Franco-Prussian War beyond the setting supplied in the chapter.
Modern constitutional law on language rights beyond the chapter’s extension activities.

known_pitfalls.claim: Franz dislikes French throughout the story.
known_pitfalls.correction: He begins carelessly but values his books, teacher and language once he learns that this is the last French lesson.

known_pitfalls.claim: M. Hamel blames only the students.
known_pitfalls.correction: He includes parents and himself when he says that everyone has something to reproach themselves with.

known_pitfalls.claim: The villagers attend an ordinary ceremony.
known_pitfalls.correction: They attend to show regret, gratitude for M. Hamel and respect for their lost country.

known_pitfalls.claim: The pigeons literally begin speaking German.
known_pitfalls.correction: Franz’s question is a rhetorical protest against controlling language and identity.

recommended_example_progression: Use Think as you read Q1 to establish Franz’s initial attitude.
Use the later Think as you read question to trace changes caused by the Berlin order.
Use Understanding the text Q1 to connect language with identity.
Use Understanding the text Q2 to interpret the pigeons.
Use Noticing form to explain the past perfect.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Understanding the text Questions 1–2, Talking about the text, Working with words, Noticing form, Writing and Things to do.
